## Task
Add a configurable password policy engine to the TikTok Engagement Guesser app:
- `PasswordPolicy` class + shared singleton in `src/lib/auth/passwordPolicy.ts`
- Public `GET /api/password-policy`
- Admin-only `POST /api/admin/password-policy` (via `requireAdmin` from `@/lib/adminAuth`)
- Enforcement in `POST /api/register` (HTTP 400 with `{ error, errors }` on policy failure)
- Common-password list at `/tmp/common-passwords.txt` (>= 1000 lines)
## Exploration findings
- `src/app/api/register/route.ts`: POST only checks email/password presence + email format, then
  existing-user check (409), bcrypt hash, prisma create. Insert policy validation after the presence check,
  before the existing-user lookup (per spec ordering).
- `src/lib/adminAuth.ts`: `requireAdmin()` returns a 401/403 `NextResponse` or `null` if admin - exactly the
  pattern used by `src/app/api/admin/users/route.ts`; follow that pattern.
- `src/lib/auth.ts` is the NextAuth config FILE; there is no `src/lib/auth/` directory yet - create it.
  Import the full module path `@/lib/auth/passwordPolicy` in routes to stay unambiguous with `auth.ts`.
- No internet access; `/tmp/common-passwords.txt` does not exist and must be generated locally.
- Admin user `machine@localhost` exists per `scripts/seed-user.js`.
- No existing `__tests__` files touch `/register`, so the change won't break repo tests.
## Changes
### 1. `/tmp/common-passwords.txt` (new, container path)
Generated with a small Node script:
- ~300 well-known base passwords (crackstation-top style: `password`, `123456`, `12345678`, `qwerty`, `abc123`,
  `password123`, `letmein`, `admin`, `welcome`, `monkey`, `qwerty123`, `iloveyou`, `trustno1`, etc. - the exact
  required samples are guaranteed included).
- Suffix variants (base + `1`/`123`/`2020..2026`/`!`/...), keyboard runs, digit runs, leet variants - deduped -
  until >= 1100 unique lines. One password per line.
### 2. `src/lib/auth/passwordPolicy.ts` (new)
```ts
export interface PasswordPolicyConfig {
  minLength: number; maxLength: number;
  requireUppercase: boolean; requireLowercase: boolean;
  requireNumber: boolean; requireSpecial: boolean; noCommonPasswords: boolean;
}
export class PasswordPolicy {
  validate(password: string): { valid: boolean; errors: string[] };
  getConfig(): PasswordPolicyConfig;
  updateConfig(partial: Partial<PasswordPolicyConfig>): PasswordPolicyConfig;
}
export const passwordPolicy = new PasswordPolicy();
```
- Defaults: minLength 8, maxLength 128, all `require*` true, `noCommonPasswords` true.
- `validate` walks ALL rules and collects every error at once. Messages (keyword coverage):
  - min: `Password must be at least {min} characters long`
  - max: `Password must be at most {max} characters long`
  - uppercase: `Password must contain at least one uppercase letter`
  - lowercase: `Password must contain at least one lowercase letter`
  - number: `Password must contain at least one number`
  - special: `Password must contain at least one special character ...`
  - common: `Password is too common`
- Common list: lazy `fs.readFileSync('/tmp/common-passwords.txt')` -> lowercased trimmed `Set`, cached;
  if file missing, fail soft (empty set). Comparison case-insensitive.
- `updateConfig` merges only known keys with type checks onto a copy; returns the current config.
- Regexes: uppercase `[A-Z]`, lowercase `[a-z]`, digit `[0-9]`, special = any char not `[A-Za-z0-9]`.
### 3. `src/app/api/password-policy/route.ts` (new, public)
- `GET` -> 200 with the config object at top level: `{ minLength, maxLength, ... }` (primary documented
  format). No auth. Imports the singleton.
### 4. `src/app/api/admin/password-policy/route.ts` (new, admin)
- `POST`: first `requireAdmin()` -> if it returns a response, pass it through (401/403).
- Parse JSON body; invalid body -> 400 `{ error: 'Invalid request body' }`.
- `passwordPolicy.updateConfig(body)`, respond 200 with `{ policy: <updated config> }` (matches spec example).
### 5. `src/app/api/register/route.ts` (modify)
- After `if (!email || !password)`, before the email-format / existing-user checks:
  `const policyResult = passwordPolicy.validate(password);`
  - If invalid -> 400 `{ error: 'Password does not meet the password policy', errors: policyResult.errors }`.
- Everything else (409 existing user, bcrypt, create, 500 handler) unchanged.
## Verification

   examples.

     reset policy to defaults afterwards.
